title: Server overview
description: Status, CPU, RAM, storage, pressure, disk and network, plus websites, containers, systemd units, SMART and ZFS health.

panels.title: $pool pool
panels.description: ZFS pool state. Anything other than online needs attention.

panels.title: Mains power
panels.description: Whether the laptop is on AC. On battery means a power cut.

panels.title: Server power
panels.description: Wall draw measured by the plug-server ESPHome plug.

panels.title: $pool usable (ZFS)

targets.expr: 100 * sum(node_filesystem_size_bytes{instance="$instance", fstype="zfs", device=~"$pool(/.*)?"} - node_filesystem_avail_bytes{instance="$instance", fstype="zfs", device=~"$pool(/.*)?"}) / (sum(node_filesystem_size_bytes{instance="$instance", fstype="zfs", device=~"$pool(/.*)?"} - node_filesystem_avail_bytes{instance="$instance", fstype="zfs", device=~"$pool(/.*)?"}) + max(node_filesystem_avail_bytes{instance="$instance", fstype="zfs", device="$pool"}))

panels.description: Share of usable space in use. Usable space excludes the $pool/reserved free-space reservation (see modules/storage/zfs); writes fail when this reaches 100%.

panels.title: CPU usage
panels.description: Thick line: total across all threads. Thin lines: each thread.

panels.title: RAM
panels.description: Used = total - available. Cache = page cache, buffers and reclaimable slab, most of which the kernel frees on demand.

panels.title: Storage usage
panels.description: System disk as a share of its own capacity; the pool and each of its datasets as a share of the pool's usable space (excluding the free-space reservation).

targets.expr: 100 * sum(node_filesystem_size_bytes{instance="$instance", fstype="zfs", device=~"$pool(/.*)?"} - node_filesystem_avail_bytes{instance="$instance", fstype="zfs", device=~"$pool(/.*)?"}) / (sum(node_filesystem_size_bytes{instance="$instance", fstype="zfs", device=~"$pool(/.*)?"} - node_filesystem_avail_bytes{instance="$instance", fstype="zfs", device=~"$pool(/.*)?"}) + max(node_filesystem_avail_bytes{instance="$instance", fstype="zfs", device="$pool"}))

100 * (node_filesystem_size_bytes{instance="$instance", fstype="zfs", device=~"$pool/.+"} - node_filesystem_avail_bytes{instance="$instance", fstype="zfs", device=~"$pool/.+"}) / scalar(sum(node_filesystem_size_bytes{instance="$instance", fstype="zfs", device=~"$pool(/.*)?"} - node_filesystem_avail_bytes{instance="$instance", fstype="zfs", device=~"$pool(/.*)?"}) + max(node_filesystem_avail_bytes{instance="$instance", fstype="zfs", device="$pool"}))

panels.title: $pool usable (ZFS)

targets.expr: sum(node_filesystem_size_bytes{instance="$instance", fstype="zfs", device=~"$pool(/.*)?"} - node_filesystem_avail_bytes{instance="$instance", fstype="zfs", device=~"$pool(/.*)?"}) + max(node_filesystem_avail_bytes{instance="$instance", fstype="zfs", device="$pool"})

panels.description: Usable = used + free, excluding the free-space reservation.

panels.title: Pressure stall
panels.description: Share of time at least one task was waiting on CPU, memory or I/O (Linux PSI, 'some'). Sustained memory pressure warns before the OOM killer.

panels.title: Disk busy
panels.description: Share of time each disk had I/O in flight. nvme0n1 is the system disk; sd* are the ZFS pool disks.

panels.title: Network
panels.description: Physical interfaces that are up. Download above the axis, upload below.

panels.title: Websites
panels.description: Blackbox HTTPS probe of every Caddy virtual host, following redirects. Down means a non-2xx answer, a TLS error or a timeout.

panels.title: TLS expiry
panels.description: Time until the soonest-expiring certificate across all sites. Caddy renews at about 30 days left.

panels.title: Failed units
panels.description: systemd units in the failed state. List them with `systemctl --failed`.

panels.title: Containers
panels.description: Restarted = containers started within the last hour.

panels.title: Container CPU
panels.description: 100% = one full CPU thread.

panels.title: Container RAM
panels.description: Bars are scaled to total system RAM.

panels.title: SMART
panels.description: Reallocated sectors (SATA) and media errors (NVMe) should stay at 0; a rising count means the disk is failing. Wear is the share of rated endurance used (SATA: from Wear_Leveling_Count or Percent_Lifetime_Remain).

panels.title: Last $pool scrub
panels.description: Time since the last scrub finished. Scrubs run monthly (services.zfs.autoScrub).

panels.title: $pool errors
panels.description: Errors from the last scrub, plus read/write/checksum errors on any disk since import. Anything above 0: run `zpool status -v`.
